items.originalTitle: Pierre Gasly on Franco Colapinto fan pressure: “Once you deal with Helmut Marko, anything else is no pressure”
detailZh: 皮埃尔·加斯利关于弗朗哥·科拉平托粉丝压力的看法：“一旦你处理了赫尔穆特·马克，其他任何压力都不算什么”
阿尔卑斯车手皮埃尔·加斯利在网上遭到了一些弗朗哥·科拉平托粉丝的辱骂，但他表示欢迎数千名阿根廷粉丝在英特拉戈斯创造的气氛
英特拉戈斯是弗朗哥·科拉平托距离主场大奖赛最近的地方，皮埃尔·加斯利知道这周末在圣保罗的阿尔卑斯车库里会营造出怎样的气氛
自从科拉平托在2024年结束了该国23年的等待，让一名车手重返赛道以来，阿根廷国旗在一级方程式大奖赛的看台上已成为一种常见的景象。这种速度和规模的反应超出了预期，即使在联系这项运动的历史可以追溯到首届世界锦标赛的国家也是如此。尽管努力将大奖赛带回阿根廷仍在继续，但成千上万的粉丝已经习惯于越过边境来观看科拉平托在英特拉戈斯的比赛。
这种支持也带来了一些社交媒体上的丑陋一面，一些自称为科拉平托支持者的账户对其他车手以及阿尔卑斯车队进行了侮辱。自从科拉平托加入车队以来，加斯利时不时地成为这种攻击的目标，最近一次是在西班牙大奖赛之后。
加斯利认为在圣保罗面对如此多的阿根廷粉丝是一种积极的体验，尤其是对他队友来说。
“我认为我们全球都有阿根廷人。我可以说可能更多在巴西，因为那里更近。你可以感受到这种支持，这就是Franco所说的。对他来说，这感觉就像在家乡的比赛一样，”加斯利说。
当被问及在Interlagos的阿根廷粉丝数量是否会在本周末给他带来压力时，加斯利笑着回答：“我在F1已经10年了，一旦你处理过Helmut Marko，其他任何事都不会有压力！”
“我知道我作为工作的任务是什么，我专注于那一点。我认为这通常是F1的美丽之处，我在这些时刻实际上能获得很多能量。”
“我喜欢被逗弄，成为一个能够回归的人。当我处于赛道上时，我总是全力以赴。巴西是一个我得到很多支持的地方，所以对我来说这也是很好的能量。”
科拉平托针对与他粉丝群体相关的网络虐待发表了评论，他在上个月发布在社交媒体上的视频中讨论了这个问题。阿根廷人在周四表示，自那以后情况有所改善，尽管他强调这是整个社区需要继续努力的事情。
“是的，情况有所改善。我认为我们都看到了这一点，所以这是一个集体努力，而不仅仅是我的努力，”他说。“但是，是的，我已经谈过了这个话题，我认为显然，作为一个社区，我们必须继续改进，但我认为一切都在正轨上。”
detailEn: Pierre Gasly on Franco Colapinto fan pressure: “Once you deal with Helmut Marko, anything else is no pressure”
The Alpine driver has faced online abuse from some Franco Colapinto supporters but says he welcomes the atmosphere created by thousands of Argentine fans at Interlagos
Interlagos is the closest Franco Colapinto gets to a home grand prix, and Pierre Gasly  knows the atmosphere that creates around the Alpine garage in Sao Paulo this weekend.

Argentina's flag has become a familiar sight in Formula 1 grandstands since Colapinto ended the country's 23-year wait for a driver on the grid in 2024. The speed and scale of the response exceeded expectations, even in a country whose ties to the sport stretch back to the inaugural world championship. And while efforts to bring a grand prix back to Argentina continue, thousands of fans have made a habit of crossing the border to watch Colapinto race at Interlagos.

That support has also had an uglier side on social media, where some accounts identifying as Colapinto supporters have directed abuse at other drivers and Alpine itself. Gasly has been on the receiving end of it from time to time since Colapinto joined the team, most recently after the Spanish Grand Prix.
Gasly sees the prospect of racing in front of so many Argentine fans in Sao Paulo as a positive, especially for his team-mate.

"I think we have Argentinians all over the world. I would say probably more in Brazil because it's closer. You can definitely feel the support and that's what Franco was saying. For him, it feels the closest to the home race," Gasly said.

Asked whether the number of Argentine fans at Interlagos might put him under pressure this weekend, Gasly laughed: "I've been 10 years in F1 and once you deal with Helmut Marko, anything else is no pressure!"
"I know what I've got to do as my job and I focus on that. I think generally it's the beauty of F1 and I get actually quite good energy in these types of moments.
"I like to be teased and be someone that comes back. I always give my best when I'm on track. Brazil is a place where I get a lot of support, so it's very good energy for me as well."

Colapinto has spoken out against online abuse linked to his fan base, addressing the issue in a video he posted on social media last month. The Argentine said on Thursday that he had seen an improvement since then, though he stressed that it was something the wider community needed to keep working on.

"Yes, it improved. I think we all saw that it improved, so it's a collective effort, not just mine," he said. "But yeah, I already spoke about the topic, and I think that obviously, as a community, we have to keep improving, but I think everything is a bit more on track."
keyPointsZh: 科拉平托在Interlagos赛道感受到了家乡般的热情。
科拉平托成为阿根廷23年来首位登上F1赛道的车手。
粉丝的反应速度和规模超出了预期。
keyPointsEn: Franco Colapinto experiences a home grand prix atmosphere at Interlagos.
Colapinto is the first Argentine driver to start a Formula 1 race in 23 years.
The fan response was faster and larger than expected.

items.titleZh: 拉塞尔因罚退无缘杆位，放弃最快圈仍感刺痛
items.summaryZh: 拉塞尔在因罚退五位而无法从杆位起步的情况下，仍在雨中的英特拉格斯排位赛中放弃了一圈本可能最快的圈速，这让他感到格外受伤。
items.originalTitle: Why Russell's 'pole' was lost either way - and it hurt like hell
items.summaryEn: George Russell was already set to miss out on pole position due to a five-place grid penalty, yet abandoning a lap that could have been quickest in the wet Interlagos qualifying session left him feeling unusually hurt.
detailZh: 乔治·拉塞尔知道自己因罚退无法从2026年巴西大奖赛的杆位起步，但即便如此，错失最快圈速仍让他感到格外受伤。
拉塞尔在延迟的雨中英特拉格斯排位赛结束后确信，他的梅赛德斯F1车队让他放弃了一圈“肯定”会是最快的圈速。
这种确信可以理解，但可能过于乐观。由于五位罚退，他本来就不会从杆位起步；但即便他不放弃，他也注定会错失最快圈，因为那一圈几乎肯定会被他的好友亚历山大·阿尔本无意中影响。
然而，真正让拉塞尔如此受伤的，是更深层东西的失去——在一个曾寄予厚望却令人失望的赛季中，一次罕见的明显优势时刻。
拉塞尔的比赛工程师马库斯·达德利建议他收油的唯一原因是，拉塞尔已经追上了阿尔本的威廉姆斯赛车——拉塞尔甚至抱怨阿尔本在单圈中途挡了他的路。
虽然拉塞尔看起来确实有望完成一个比最终杆位得主兰多·诺里斯更快的单圈，因为他在放弃该圈时至少快了百分之几秒，但这依赖于他在完成该圈时拥有畅通无阻的赛道，而拉塞尔本不会拥有这样的条件。
拉塞尔与阿尔本的距离足够近，以至于他已经连续三个迷你赛段比上一圈更慢。他可能会在中段末尾的左手11号弯受到干扰，随后是通往终点线长上坡的容桑左弯，以及进入起终点直道的弯角。
梅赛德斯车队负责人托托·沃尔夫表示，拉塞尔“当时比诺里斯略快一点，但正在追上阿尔本，我们认为他即将损失时间”。而这一威胁是真实存在的。
即使阿尔本以比第一轮通过最后赛段更快的速度完成了那一圈，他也会比拉塞尔和诺里斯能做出的成绩慢上零点几秒。
实际情况是，阿尔本在进入茹桑库弯时严重锁死，损失了大量时间，但没有冲出赛道，这意味着他最好的情况是在出弯时挡住拉塞尔，让梅赛德斯赛车通过，或者更可能的是，完全挡住拉塞尔的路线。
无论哪种情况，拉塞尔都会被限制在阿尔本的峰值速度或他降低后的速度之内——这两种情况都无法让拉塞尔足够快地完成那一圈以击败诺里斯。
同样值得指出的是，拉塞尔那句“移动啊阿尔博诺！”的无线电消息，才是促使达德利开始讨论放弃该圈的关键触发点。
也许梅赛德斯无论如何都会介入。但拉塞尔一定知道阿尔本极有可能毁掉这一圈，否则他就不会表达自己的不满。
所以，在某种程度上，他会意识到那一圈非常好的成绩正在溜走。正如赛道工程总监安德鲁·肖夫林所指出的，如果拉塞尔完成该圈并被阻挡，继续行驶会“有风险危及那一圈和下一圈”。
沃尔夫表示，“事后看来，考虑到下一圈会下雨，我们应该继续跑，但事后说这话很容易”——这在一定程度上适用，因为他们至少可以或应该尝试完成该圈，但这可能并未改变结果。
真正的不幸最终是与阿尔本距离过近，而不是梅赛德斯如何处理此事。
从拉塞尔的无线电通话、他在赛后封闭区接受电视采访时的初步评论，到最后的官方新闻发布会，他的沮丧程度已经完整地展现出来。
当沃尔夫试图在无线电中安抚拉塞尔不断上升的怒火，说“乔治，你是第二名”时，你几乎能听到拉塞尔在回复时努力消化自己的懊恼：“是啊，但是……第二名。我不想当第二名，我想当第一名。那一圈本该是第一名的圈速。”
“天哪！”
在输给安东内利、无缘冠军的过程中，拉塞尔有过不少出色的排位赛表现，即便在较弱的周末，他也常常能把自己拉回竞争行列。
拉塞尔在2026款赛车上常常缺乏自然的感觉，有时就是对它信心不足。即便他曾经接近安东内利或略微领先，对他来说也从来不像安东内利状态好时那样轻松。
在巴西的干地练习中，他似乎又一次落后于安东内利，但下雨之后情况就变了。这正变成少数几次他干脆利落地成为更快的梅赛德斯车手的情况之一，看起来他拥有澳大利亚、西班牙、阿塞拜疆那种掌控力。
所以，尽管他本来保不住杆位，尽管这仅仅改变了他从第六还是第七位起步，拉塞尔真的很想要这个。
无论这是为了他自己、为了向外界展示些什么，或许甚至是为了某种内在的东西，这都会是他自身出色巅峰状态的有力信号——而此时此刻，所有焦点都集中在安东内利的冠军、安东内利的才华，以及拉塞尔那种坏运气与短板交织的处境上。
拉塞尔说：“显然，从车队方面来说，我们本周末有一个目标，那就是赢得总冠军，这非常符合车队每个人的目标。”
“对我个人而言，考虑到上周的情况，今天拿到杆位对我来说意义重大。”
“上周我以九毫秒之差错过了杆位，但那真是一个惊喜。今天，我真的感觉我跑的每一圈，在我完成的大多数圈数里我都排在榜首。”
“所以，我对最终的结果真的非常非常失望。”
detailEn: George Russell knew he would not start the 2026 Brazilian Grand Prix from pole position due to a grid penalty, yet missing out on being quickest left him feeling unusually hurt regardless.
Russell ended the delayed, wet Interlagos qualifying session convinced his Mercedes Formula 1 team had made him abandon a lap that was “definitely” going to be quickest.

That certainty was understandable, but probably overzealous. He would never have started from pole anyway, thanks to his five-place grid drop, but he was poised to miss out regardless of backing off because the lap was almost certainly about to be inadvertently compromised by Russell’s good friend Alex Albon.
What hurt Russell so much, though, was the loss of something deeper – a rare moment of obvious superiority in a season that promised so much and yet has been so disappointing.

The only reason Russell’s race engineer Marcus Dudley advised him to back off was because Russell had caught Alex Albon’s Williams – and Russell had even complained about Albon being in his way in the middle of the lap.

While Russell did seem to be on his way to completing a faster lap than eventual polesitter Lando Norris, as he was at least a few hundredths quicker at the moment he aborted, that relies on a clear run to end the lap that Russell would not have had.

Russell was close enough to Albon that he had already posted three mini-sectors in a row slower than his previous lap. He would have potentially been disturbed through the left-hand Turn 11 at the end of the middle sector, then the Juncao left-hander that leads to the long, uphill run to the finish line, and the kink onto the start-finish straight.
Mercedes boss Toto Wolff said Russell was “very slightly up on Norris at that point but was catching Albon and we thought was about to lose time”. And the threat was real.
Even if Albon completed the lap he was on at an improved pace compared to his first run through the final sector, he would be several tenths slower than what Russell and Norris could do.

As it was, Albon had a major lock-up into Juncao that cost him a load of time, but did not send him off-track, making it likely he would have at best held Russell up on the exit as the Mercedes went by or, probably more likely, got in Russell’s way completely.
Either way, Russell would have been contained at Albon’s peak pace or his reduced pace – neither of which would have let Russell finish the lap quickly enough to beat Norris.
It’s also worth pointing out that Russell’s “move Albono!” radio message was the trigger for Dudley to even initiate talk of aborting the lap in question.
Perhaps Mercedes would have interjected anyway. But Russell must have known that Albon was at serious risk of ruining the lap otherwise he would not have expressed his frustration.

So, on some level, he would have known that very good lap was slipping away. And as trackside engineering director Andrew Shovlin pointed out, continuing would “risk compromising both that lap and the next” if Russell had completed the lap and been baulked.

Wolff said that “in hindsight, with the rain coming on the next lap, we should have kept going but it is very easy to say this after the event” – which applies insofar as they could or should have at least tried to finish the lap, but it probably did not change the outcome.
The real misfortune was ultimately the proximity to Albon, rather than how Mercedes handled it.

Between Russell’s in-car radio messages, his initial comments on television during the parc ferme interviews post-session, and finally the official press conference, the magnitude of his frustration became fully formed.

When Wolff tried to soothe Russell’s rising anger over the radio with “George you’re P2”, you could almost hear Russell trying to process his own annoyance as he replied: ““Yeah but…P2. I don’t wanna be P2, I want to be P1. That was a P1 lap.
“F*****g hell!”
Russell’s had plenty of good qualifying performances through his championship defeat to Kimi Antonelli, as even on weaker weekends he’s often been able to haul himself into contention.

Russell has often lacked a natural feeling in the 2026 car, and sometimes just not had enough confidence in it. Even when he’s been close to Antonelli or marginally ahead, it has never looked as easy for him as when Antonelli’s on form.

He also seemed to be trailing Antonelli yet again in the dry in practice in Brazil, but when the rain came the situation changed. This was turning into one of the few occasions where he has just been emphatically the faster Mercedes driver and looked like he had an Australia/Spain/Azerbaijan-type control.
So, regardless of the fact he would not have kept pole, regardless of how it only changed whether he starts sixth or seventh, Russell really wanted this.

Whether it was for himself, something to show the outside world, or maybe even something internal, it would have been a strong signal of his own brilliant peak, at a time when all the focus has been on Antonelli’s title, Antonelli’s brilliance, and Russell’s mix of bad luck and shortcomings.
“Obviously, from the team side, we've got one goal this weekend, which is to win the championship, and that's very much the goal of everyone within the team,” Russell said.
“For me personally, given the circumstances of last week, it would have meant a lot to me to take pole today.
“I missed it last week by nine milliseconds, but that was a real surprise. Today, I really felt every lap I was doing, I was top of the leaderboard most laps I completed.
“So, I'm really, really disappointed with how that panned out.”

items.originalTitle: 'Of course there is tension' - how Leclerc sees Ferrari Mexico fallout
items.summaryEn: Leclerc said Ferrari's internal tension after the Mexican Grand Prix has been settled through talks, and he believes the matter has been blown out of proportion and should not be discussed further.
detailZh: 当刘易斯·汉密尔顿和弗雷德·瓦塞尔在巴西面对关于法拉利墨西哥大奖赛风波、以及需要怎样做才能确保汉密尔顿和夏尔·勒克莱尔真正互相竞争而不损害车队利益的一连串问题时，勒克莱尔的观点基本上没有出现在讨论中。
由于上周第一个孩子出生，他较晚才加入这场讨论，这可以理解；用他自己的话说：“我把比安卡抱在怀里的那段时间，脑子里没有太多别的或其他的东西，这种情况大概一直持续到周四晚上我抵达、该和弗雷德、刘易斯谈话的时候。”
周五练习后的媒体区有过简短评论，勒克莱尔当时说，在这些内部谈话后，他认为此事“完全解决”，并且“我认为我们今后不应该再过多谈论它”。
周六排位赛后，勒克莱尔不得不应对更多试图让他就此敞开心扉的问题，而他基本上坚持了同样的说法。
“当然，从我的角度来看，我非常直接，我认为能谈一谈是件好事，”他说。“我认为在这样的时刻之后，这总是必要的。”
“我认为这件事被放得太大了，但它也已经存在太久了。”
“与此同时，这对我来说是非常特别的一周，所以我之前无法真正进行那些讨论，而进行那些讨论很重要，但现在我认为那是一个已经翻篇的章节，我认为向前看将很重要。”
但是，尽管勒克莱尔试图让F1世界从上周日在墨西哥发生的事情中走出来，他同时也证实了他与汉密尔顿之间的竞争紧张关系，而瓦塞尔肯定要费一番功夫去处理。
当被问及他和汉密尔顿之间现在是否一切正常时，勒克莱尔说“是的，当然”，随后补充道：“当然会有紧张，当然我们都想跑在对方前面，有时我们不会把事情做对，有时在看待事情的方式上意见不合也没关系，但同时讨论这些会有很大帮助。”
“有时候你们意见不合，就必须找到共同点。”
目前看来，共同点已经找到了，至少在对外的公开层面是如此。
汉密尔顿在排位赛后对天空体育表示：“我和查尔斯坐下来谈了谈，我们把问题解决了，然后继续前进。”
“我们彼此仍然非常尊重，我很高兴我们聊了聊，现在事情翻篇了。
“我们一直像平常一样相处得很好，所以有时候在这种情形下，只需要谈一谈就行。
“双方都没有提出任何要求，只是……我们都提出了自己的观点，以及我们可以做得更好、相互支持的方面，是的，希望接下来的比赛能更好。”
所以看起来汉密尔顿和勒克莱尔现在正处于风暴后的平静之中，但不需要太多事情就能让那些紧张情绪再次浮现，并再次考验法拉利的耐心。
detailEn: As Lewis Hamilton and Fred Vasseur have faced a barrage of questions about Ferrari’s Mexican Grand Prix debacle in Brazil, and what needs to be done to ensure Hamilton and Charles Leclerc can actually race one another without hurting the team’s interests, Leclerc’s view has been basically absent from the debate.

He’s been understandably late to this discussion, owing to the birth of his first child this past week, and in his own words “the time where I've had Bianca in my arms, there wasn't much more or much else in my head, and that's been the case until probably Thursday night when I arrived and when it was time to speak with Fred and Lewis”.

There was a brief comment in the media pen after Friday practice, when Leclerc said he considered the matter “fully settled” following those internal talks, and that “I don’t think we should be speaking about it too much going forward”.
After qualifying on Saturday Leclerc had to field several more questions aimed at getting him to open up on this matter, and he pretty much stuck to the same script.
“From my perspective I was very straightforward of course and I think it was good to speak,” he said. “I think this is always needed after a moment like this.
“I think it took proportions that are way too big, but it has been around also for way too long.

“At the same time it was a very special week for me so I couldn't really have those discussions before and it was important to have those discussions, but now I consider that a closed chapter and I think it will be important to look ahead.”

But as much as Leclerc was trying to move the F1 world on from what happened last Sunday in Mexico, he also in the same breath confirmed the competitive tension between himself and Hamilton that Vasseur is surely going to have his work cut out trying to manage.

Leclerc said “yes of course” when asked if everything was now OK between him and Hamilton, before adding: “Of course there is tension, of course we want to finish ahead of each other and sometimes we are not going to do things right, and it's OK sometimes to disagree on the way you see things, but at the same time discussing about those helps a whole lot.
“Sometimes you disagree and you've got to find a common ground.”
For now it would seem common ground has been found, at least publicly facing.
Hamilton told Sky F1 after qualifying that “me and Charles, we sat and spoke and we squashed it, and we’re moving on.
“We still have a huge amount of respect for each other, and I’m glad we had a chat, and now we move on.
“We’ve been getting along just fine as normal, so sometimes in those scenarios it just takes having a conversation.
"There’s been no demands from either side, it’s just been…we’ve both given our points and areas that we can do better and support each other and yeah, hoping to have better races moving forwards.”
So it would seem Hamilton and Leclerc are now in the calm after the storm, but it won’t take much for those tensions to re-emerge and test Ferrari’s patience once more.
keyPointsZh: 勒克莱尔因第一个孩子出生而较晚参与讨论，直到抵达巴西后的周四晚才与瓦塞尔和汉密尔顿交谈
他在周五练习后的媒体区称此事已“完全解决”，周六排位后重申立场不变

items.originalTitle: Liam Lawson rues Brazilian GP qualifying mistake despite third-place grid start
items.summaryEn: Lawson advanced to Q3 in wet qualifying in Sao Paulo and qualified fifth, but will start third thanks to other drivers' penalties. Despite this, he was still unhappy with his own mistake in qualifying.
detailZh: 劳森对巴西站排位赛失误感到遗憾，尽管将从第三位发车
这位小红牛车手在圣保罗排位赛位列第五，因其他车手受罚将在正赛从第三位起步，但他仍对结果感到不满
劳森认为自己的速度足以在圣保罗拿下头排发车位，但他对自己在排位赛中的“失误”感到遗憾，这意味着他只能从第三位发车。
这位新西兰人在雨地排位赛中表现出色，再次晋级Q3，随后与顶级车队的车手争夺前列位置。在排位赛最后一节中，他是较早出场的车手之一，仅晚于费尔南多·阿隆索，并且初期圈速名列前茅。
随着本节练习临近结束时更多降雨到来，车手们尽早完成有效圈至关重要，而劳森的第一轮尝试最终让他位列发车位第三。但他认为自己本可以更高，甚至有可能排在基米·安东内利之前——后者以第三名完赛——只要他在出场圈与阿隆索保持了更大的距离。
“我认为作为车手，你总想最大化发挥，我觉得我们今天没有完全做到，”他在本节结束后对天空体育表示。“我们一出场状态就很好。显然我们在维修区通道上有点运气，我们的位置比顶级车队更靠后。所以我出场后，在第一圈追上了费尔南多太多，不得不放弃第二圈。
“然后我就没能真正最大化发挥。”
劳森在排位赛成绩上比安东内利慢0.226秒——而击败这位新加冕的世界冠军本足以让这位新西兰人获得头排发车位，因为排位赛中做出第二快圈速的乔治·拉塞尔在周末早些时候已受到引擎罚退。
当被问及是否相信能在头排取得排位赛成绩时，劳森回答说：“我的意思是，作为一名车手，我会说有可能，但显然你永远不知道。而且当时雨正在下。所以等我跑到那一圈结束时……你永远说不准。”
“我不知道其他人是什么时候完成的。但是，考虑到我们只跑了一圈，我认为我们做得不错。”
尽管如此，在做出第五快的时间后，由于拉塞尔和夏尔·勒克莱尔的罚退，他将在发车格上前进两个位置。
“这仍然是一个不错的起步位置，”他对媒体说。“显然，我总是接受这些免费的位置提升，但作为一名车手，你也总是希望最大化利用机会。”
“我觉得无论如何，这里的比赛都会很艰难。我认为不太可能完全干地。但我觉得我们在任何条件下都有一辆快车。”
这位新西兰人今年继续给人留下深刻印象，但他下赛季仍未与车队签订合同。
detailEn: Liam Lawson rues Brazilian GP qualifying mistake despite third-place grid start
The Racing Bulls driver qualified fifth in Sao Paulo and will start third thanks to other drivers' penalties – yet he was still unhappy with the result
Liam Lawson reckons he had enough pace to earn a front-row grid spot in Sao Paulo – but rues his own "mistake" in qualifying, which meant he'll have to start from P3.

The New Zealander starred in wet qualifying, once again progressing into Q3 – and then fighting for the front positions with drivers from the top teams. In the final segment of the session, he was one of the first out on track, only behind Fernando Alonso – and was among the quickest early on.

With more rain coming towards the end of the session, it was important for the drivers to put laps together early, and Lawson's first attempt ultimately put him P3 on the grid. Yet he believes he could've been higher and potentially ahead of Kimi Antonelli, who qualified third – if only he'd left a bigger gap to Alonso on his out-lap.

"I think as a driver you want to maximise it and I feel like we didn't quite today," he told Sky Sports after the session. "We're in a really good place out of the box. Obviously we get lucky with the pit lane that we're further down than the top teams. So I went out there and then I caught Fernando too much on the first lap and had to abort the second one.
"And then I didn't get to really maximise it."

Lawson was 0.226s slower than Antonelli in the qualifying classification – and beating the newly crowned world champion would've been enough for the New Zealander to earn a front-row start, as George Russell, who set the second-fastest time in qualifying, had received an engine penalty earlier in the weekend.

When asked whether he believed qualifying on the front row was possible, Lawson replied: "I mean, as a driver, I'm going to say yes, but obviously you never know. And obviously the rain was coming down. So by the time I got to the end of the lap... You never know.
"I don't know when everybody else did it. But, yeah, considering we got one lap, I think we did a good job."
Still, having set the fifth-fastest time, he'll move two positions up the grid thanks to Russell and Charles Leclerc's penalties.
"It's still a good place to start," he said to the media. "Obviously, I always take the free positions, but you always want to maximise as a driver as well.
"I think either way it's going to be a tough race here. I think unlikely it's going to be fully dry. But I think we have a quick car in all conditions."
The New Zealander, who continues to impress this year, still doesn't have a contract with the team for next season.

items.originalTitle: George Russell's Brazilian GP qualifying fury explained: "Pole was there for the taking"
items.summaryEn: George Russell has explained his radio fury over a miscommunication with Mercedes, which he claimed cost him pole position for the Brazilian Grand Prix to Lando Norris.
detailZh: 拉塞尔解释巴西大奖赛排位赛愤怒：“杆位本可到手”
拉塞尔解释了自己在无线电中对梅赛德斯沟通失误的愤怒，他称这次失误让诺里斯抢走了F1巴西大奖赛的杆位。
与巴西大奖赛受天气影响的排位赛主题一致，拉塞尔在赛后新闻发布会上面对F1媒体时脸色阴沉。
冠军已经无望，因更换引擎被罚退后五位发车意味着拉塞尔周日原本就不可能从前排起步。但在一个充满挑战的赛季结束时，即便带有罚退，拿下又一个杆位在心理层面依然重要，哪怕只是为了给更强的2027赛季打下基础。
英特拉格斯混乱的雨地排位赛给了拉塞尔这个机会。当第三节排位赛条件再次开始恶化时，拉塞尔率先用半雨胎做出第一轮成绩，比兰多·诺里斯最初的标杆成绩快了四成。
刚跑出足以暂列杆位的圈速后，他的比赛工程师马库斯·达德利就催促他在条件恶化前再跑一圈：“能推就推，我觉得这场雨来之前我们还能再跑一圈。”
随后拉塞尔在第二赛段追上了亚历克斯·阿尔本驾驶的威廉姆斯车尾，急切地想让这位朋友让开：“让开，阿尔本诺！”
但当达德利暗示拉塞尔还有机会再开始一个飞驰圈时，混乱出现了，他必须在接近12号弯——棘手的茹卡奥弯，众多赛车曾在此滑上湿草——时迅速做出决定。
乔治·拉塞尔，梅赛德斯，亚历山大·阿尔本，威廉姆斯
“你得告诉我，伙计，我该怎么做。我是收油还是继续冲？”拉塞尔在无线电里说。
回复立刻传来：“我们现在可以收油了，现在收油，”拉塞尔并不信服，要求确认。
就在那一刻，诺里斯冲过终点线完成第二个计时圈，比拉塞尔的标杆成绩快了两成，抢走了杆位。而随着条件迅速恶化，拉塞尔意识到放弃自己这一圈的决定是错的，一个挽回颜面的杆位机会已经没了。
在经历了今年已经发生的一切之后，这件事他很难接受。
“兄弟，你他妈让我收油。搞什么鬼！”拉塞尔发泄道。“乔治，你是第二名，”车队领队托托·沃尔夫的介入并不令人满意，拉塞尔回答说：“我不想当第二名，我想当第一名。那一圈是能拿第一的圈。真他妈见鬼。”
从封闭车检区到强制的前三名新闻发布会之间的短暂间隔，几乎没有缓解他的失望。
“我觉得只是有点沟通不畅。我需要和车队谈谈，因为我们以为在雨来之前还能再跑一圈，”拉塞尔解释道。“我当时那一圈非常强，却被要求收油，因为我追上了阿尔本，然后显然雨就来了。
“这非常令人失望。我们需要弄清楚这是怎么发生的，以及为什么我们会做出错误的判断。但整节练习中我都感觉非常强劲。我确实觉得杆位本就在掌握之中。”
“一旦做出决定，我想我们就知道那是错误的选择，因为他们已经能切实感觉到雨下得更大了。”
不过，拉塞尔不愿让自己的比赛工程师成为众矢之的，因为在混合条件下做出这种瞬间决定，是维修区内错综复杂的团队协作的产物。
“我们不能指责任何人。我们需要弄清楚为什么做出了那个决定，以及我们的系统是否告诉了我们所需的信息，因为你依赖的是雷达，”他说。
这不是我工程师的错。他最终是那个传递信息的人，但他有12个人在跟他说话，把信息给他转达。所以我们只需要理解为什么我们做出了那个决定。
之后在接受天空体育采访时，沃尔夫并不认为拉塞尔能守住杆位，因为12号弯的条件比诺里斯片刻之前经过时明显恶化。
“你知道，如果我们有水晶球能知道是否该收油，那会有帮助，”他说。“这很难，是五五开的判断。
“他当时正赶上阿尔本，在那个阶段比诺里斯快18毫秒，所以我认为那不足以拿到杆位。但显然他在各节练习与排位中都开得很完美，他配得上杆位。”
拉塞尔依然斗志昂扬，他希望周日的比赛能在类似条件下进行，因为他将从第七位而不是第二位发车。队友基米·安东内利在排位赛中位列第三，将与诺里斯并排发车，他未能匹配拉塞尔的速度。
其他前排竞争者马克斯·维斯塔潘和刘易斯·汉密尔顿将从队尾发车，不太可能成为影响因素，而夏尔·勒克莱尔和奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里将从车阵中游起步。
“在雨中我感觉非常自信。我认为我和兰多的速度是场上最好的，”拉塞尔宣称。“我希望明天是湿地。我觉得如果下雨，我有更大的机会。”
detailEn: George Russell's Brazilian GP qualifying fury explained: "Pole was there for the taking"
George Russell has explained his radio fury over a miscommunication with Mercedes, which he claimed had cost him pole at Formula 1's Brazilian Grand Prix to Lando Norris

In keeping with the theme of the Brazilian Grand Prix's weather-hit qualifying, George Russell had a thunderous look on his face when he faced the Formula 1 media in the post-session press conference.

The title has gone and a five-place grid penalty for an engine swap meant Russell was never going to start on the front row on Sunday. But at the end of a challenging year, it was still mentally important to claim another pole - with or without grid penalty - if only to lay the foundations for a stronger 2027.

Interlagos' frantic wet-weather qualifying gave Russell that opportunity. As conditions started to worsen again in Q3, Russell led the first salvo of runs on intermediates, and took four tenths out of Lando Norris' initial benchmark.

Right after setting a lap which was good enough for provisional pole, his race engineer Marcus Dudley urged him to carry on for another lap before conditions worsened: "Push if you can, I think we'll get one more lap before this rain."
Russell then caught the back of Alex Albon's Williams in the second sector, willing his friend out of the way: "Move, Albono!"

But when Dudley suggested Russell would have the opportunity to start one more flyer, confusion set in and a quick call had to be made as he approached Turn 12, the tricky Juncao corner which saw numerous cars slide onto the wet grass.
George Russell, Mercedes, Alexander Albon, Williams
"You need to tell me, mate, what I'm doing. Am I backing or going?" Russell said over the radio.
The reply came instantly: "We can back up now, back up now," with an unconvinced Russell asking for confirmation.

It was at that very moment that Norris crossed the line for a second timed lap, and took two tenths out of Russell's benchmark to snatch pole away. And with conditions worsening quickly, Russell realised the call to abandon his lap had been wrong, and a chance for a redeeming pole was gone.
After all he had been through already this year, it was not something he took well.

"Mate, you fucking told me to back off. What the hell!" Russell vented. "George, you're P2," was an unsatisfactory intervention from team principal Toto Wolff, with Russell replying: "I don't want to be P2, I want to be P1. That was a P1 lap. Fucking hell."
The short interval between parc ferme and the compulsory top-three press conference did little to dampen his disappointment.

"I think it was just a bit of miscommunication. I needed to speak with the team because we believed we'd get another lap before the rain came in," Russell explained. "I was on a really strong lap and I was asked to back off because I caught up with Albon and then obviously the rain came.
"It was very disappointing. We need to understand how it happened and why we got that wrong. But I felt very strong the whole session. I definitely felt the pole was there for the taking.
"As soon as it was made, I think we knew it was the wrong one because already they could actually feel the rain pouring harder."
Russell was keen to keep his race engineer out of the firing line, though, as such a split-second decision in mixed conditions is the product of an intricate web of teamwork in the garage.
"We can't point the finger at somebody. We need to understand why we made that decision and were our systems telling us what we needed to know because you're relying on the radar," he said.

"It's not my engineer's fault. He's ultimately the one who passes the message on, but he's got 12 people talking to him, giving him that information to relay. So we just need to understand why we made that decision."
Speaking to Sky Sports afterwards, Wolff wasn't convinced Russell could have hung on to pole given conditions were getting markedly worse in Turn 12 than they had been for Norris just moments prior.
"You know, if we were to have a crystal ball to know whether you should back off or not, then that would be helpful," he said. "A difficult one, it's a 50-50 call.

"He was running into Albon, was 18 milliseconds up on Norris at that stage, so I don't think it would have been enough for pole. But obviously he's driven perfectly all sessions and he merited to be on pole."

Russell remained combative and wants Sunday to be in similar conditions as he starts from seventh instead of second. Team-mate Kimi Antonelli will line up alongside Norris instead after qualifying third, having been unable to match Russell's pace.

Other frontrunners Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton are starting from the rear of the field and are unlikely to be a factor, while Charles Leclerc and Oscar Piastri are starting in the middle of the pack.
"I felt really confident in the rain. I think my pace along with Lando's was by far the best out there," Russell declared. "I hope it is wet tomorrow. I feel I've got a greater chance if it's wet."
keyPointsZh: 拉塞尔因更换引擎被罚退后五位发车，周日原本就不可能从前排起步。
在经历一个艰难的赛季后，拉塞尔认为即便带有罚退，拿下杆位对心理层面依然重要，可为2027赛季打下基础。
keyPointsEn: Russell had a five-place grid penalty for an engine swap, so he was never going to start from the front row on Sunday.
At the end of a challenging year, Russell felt claiming another pole was mentally important, with or without the grid penalty, if only to lay the foundations for a stronger 2027.

Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc held talks with Ferrari team principal Frederic Vasseur in Brazil following their contentious opening lap incident last time out in Mexico; watch Sunday's Sao Paulo Grand Prix live at 5pm on Sky Sports F1, build-up from 3.30pm
Highlights from qualifying for the 2026 Sao Paulo Grand Prix
Lewis Hamilton says he and Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc have "squashed" their incident at the Mexico City Grand Prix after holding talks in Brazil.

Hamilton, Leclerc and team principal Frederic Vasseur held talks on Thursday night to discuss the incident which saw Max Verstappen take advantage of the opening lap Ferrari squabble last Sunday to win the race.
Hamilton has subsequently been critical of Leclerc in interviews and said that discussions were required to more clearly define their rules of combat to avoid costly repeats in future.

Hamilton will start at the back of the grid for Sunday's Sao Paulo Grand Prix due to a power unit change and spoke to the media for the first time on Saturday since his talks with Leclerc.
"Me and Charles sat and spoke and we squashed it, and we're moving on," he told Sky Sports F1.
"We still have a huge amount of respect for each other and I'm glad we had a chat and now we move on.

"We've been getting along just fine as normal. Sometimes in those scenarios it takes having a conversation and there's been no demands from either side, it's both just giving our points and areas we can do better and support each other. I'm hoping to have better races moving forwards."
Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen reflected on a wet qualifying session in Sao Paulo
Leclerc, who starts 14th after a 10-grid place penalty for a new internal combustion engine, had a similar opinion to Hamilton.
"Obviously, there's been a lot of things, probably too much things in the last week," he said.
"We've spoken. I think everything is settled, and I'm looking forward for the rest of the weekend now."
Charles Leclerc says he's 'settled' his disagreement with Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton after their clash in last week's Mexico City GP
Vasseur: The guidelines are still the same

The Mexico incident comes two months after Leclerc admitted he was at fault for his opening lap battle with Hamilton in Monza, where the latter was forced wide into the gravel and lost several positions.
Vasseur says he reminded Hamilton and Leclerc that the team comes first and the drivers must "keep that in mind".
"The guidelines are still the same. They accumulated perhaps a bit of frustration because they are starting each weekend side by side, and you have a kind of accumulation of fact," he said.
"But at the end of the day, the guideline is always the same - it's that they need to respect each other.
Ferrari Team Principal Fred Vasseur answers questions about Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc after a public spat between the two
"They are two competitors with the fighting spirit for sure, but they need to have a respect for the other one.
"But mainly and firstly, they need to respect the brand, the team, the people working at home, the people working at the on track.
"I think we are putting a lot of effort on this, and the message was clear and will stay clear."

items.originalTitle: Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen warn of difficult F1 Brazilian GP comebacks
detailZh: 刘易斯·汉密尔顿和马克斯·维斯塔潘警告巴西F1大奖赛回归困难
刘易斯·汉密尔顿和马克斯·维斯塔潘预计在巴西大奖赛中超车将更加困难
刘易斯·汉密尔顿、法拉利、马克斯·维斯塔潘、红牛车队
法拉利车迷们。最新的法拉利F1新闻、车手更新、技术分析和来自马拉内洛及以外的比赛反应。
刘易斯·汉密尔顿和马克斯·维斯塔潘都预计在英特拉戈斯赛道超越对手将比以往赛季更加困难，因为他们准备从发车线的最后位置开始周日举行的巴西大奖赛。
两位车手都在巴西更换了新的动力单元部件，超出了本赛季的分配。因此，汉密尔顿和维斯塔潘将分别从第20位和第21位发车，只有凯迪拉克的塞尔吉奥·佩雷斯在他们后面，排在第22位。
英特拉戈斯赛道一直是一个超越相对容易的赛道。维斯塔潘和汉密尔顿都曾在赛道上从很后的位置赢得比赛：汉密尔顿在2021年从第10位起步，维斯塔潘在2024年从第17位起步。但随着2026年规则的改变，驾驶者辅助系统被取消，新的超越模式出现，他们都认为这可能不再是事实。
‘超越将会更加困难一些，’维斯塔潘在雨后的排位赛结束后对天空体育F1频道说。
“这里的超车模式实际上并没有做什么。每个人都从最后一个弯道到1号弯道在消耗电池。每个人都打开了他们的翅膀。”
“所以效果将比正常情况下要小。这会让你在到达与你有相似圈速的车辆时超车变得更难。前几辆车没问题，但其他的就会有点难了。”
汉密尔顿在接受媒体采访时补充道：“我认为会更难。因为那时候我们显然有一个非常长的直道。如果你接近，你就有DRS，也许对方没有。”
“因为现在每个人都只是打开了他们的翅膀，我认为超车将会非常非常难。我不确定你是否会看到过去看到的那种比赛。但也许湿滑的天气会改变这一点。”
detailEn: Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen warn of difficult F1 Brazilian GP comebacks
Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen expect overtaking to be more difficult at the Brazilian Grand Prix
Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari, Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing
For Ferrari fans. The latest Scuderia Ferrari F1 news, driver updates, technical analysis and race reaction from Maranello and beyond.
Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen both expect overtaking to be much harder at Interlagos than in previous seasons, as they prepare to start Sunday's Brazilian Grand Prix from the back of the grid.

Both drivers have taken new power unit parts in Brazil, exceeding their allocation for the season. As a result, Hamilton and Verstappen will start from 20th and 21st on the grid, respectively, with only Cadillac's Sergio Perez behind them in 22nd.

Interlagos has long been a track where overtaking has been relatively easy. Both Verstappen and Hamilton have won at the track from well down the order before: Hamilton from 10th in 2021 and Verstappen from 17th in 2024. But with DRS gone under the 2026 regulations and the new overtake mode, both believe this may no longer be the case.
"It's going to be a bit harder to overtake," Verstappen told Sky Sports F1 after the rain-soaked qualifying session.
"The overtake mode doesn't really do a lot around here. Everyone is draining their battery from the last corner to Turn 1. Everyone has their wings open.

"So the effect is going to be less than normal. And that will make it a bit harder to overtake once you get to the cars that are similar lap time. The first few cars is not a problem, but then the other ones will be a bit harder."

Hamilton added while speaking to the media: "I think [it will be] harder. Because back then we had, obviously, a very long straight. And if you got close, you had the DRS and maybe a car wouldn't have it.

"Because now everyone is just opening up their wings, I think overtaking will be very, very, very hard. I'm not sure you're going to see the same sort of races that you've seen in the past. But maybe the wet conditions will change that."
